# What carries into the rebuild

**Bottom line:** `refresh` is worth keeping as a *reference implementation*, not as a codebase. Roughly 8–12% of its ~8,000 lines survives literal transplant. What genuinely survives is a set of ~25 hard-won decisions, four code fragments, and one complete inventory of the product's surfaces. Everything else gets re-derived — and re-derived *differently*, because a single wrong modelling decision (`documents.clerk_user_id`) propagates into every subsystem and is the reason the tier/quota/billing/render machinery exists at all.

The adversarial pass overturned 7 of 9 verdicts, all in the same direction: assessors kept labelling things `adopt_with_changes` while writing change lists that rewrote 80–90% of the artifact. I re-verified the load-bearing claims in the repo myself. **The challengers are right on the label in every contested case except the design system, where they are right on the architecture and wrong on the output.**

## Verdict table

| Subsystem | Verdict | Confidence | Effort | One-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spec & product decisions | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 2–3 days | The engineering decisions are gold; the 1592-line document and its frame are not — and §12 contains eight rows the new design reverses. |
| DB schema & migrations | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 1–2 days | 424 lines of declarative SQLAlchemy; the hub table is condemned, the retention cascade silently destroys paid LLM summaries, and all 6 migrations are discarded anyway. |
| Job queue & scheduler | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 3–4 days | Postgres-as-queue is the right call and carries; the 328-line runtime holds an open DB transaction across every network call and cannot honour its own timeout spec. |

| Diff & citations | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 4–5 days | The materiality gate is duplicated across two files, the full diff runs twice per change, and a 67-char "we now sell your data" insert is classified cosmetic and silently dropped. |
| AI summarization | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 3–4 days | The one component the assessor said to carry verbatim — the citation validator — manufactures authoritative citations for hallucinated claims. |
| Web structure | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 1–2 weeks | Zero tests, zero error boundaries, a quota gate swallowed by a bare `catch {}`, and a BFF whose only client is the page renderer. |
| Design system | **Rebuild the look, keep the architecture** *(contested — I split it)* | High | 1–2 weeks | Every value dies (owner has rejected it); the semantic-CSS-plus-custom-properties architecture is *correct* and should be kept, with scales and a CI gate added. |
| Auth, billing & entitlements | **Rebuild** *(contested)* | High | 2–3 days | Delete billing wholesale; the HMAC boundary is 100 good lines that don't sign the principal, so "carry unchanged" imports the flaw. |

Everything is contested except the two halves nobody disputed: *Postgres-as-queue is right* and *the design must be replaced*.

## Carry over as-is

Four things. That is the honest list.

**1. The SKIP LOCKED claim query** — `apps/api/inplain/worker/jobs.py:11-32`, ~20 lines. CTE + `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` + `UPDATE … FROM claimed RETURNING`. Textbook-correct, and getting the CTE shape wrong on a second attempt is a real risk (double-claim under concurrency is the classic failure). Paste it in. Everything *around* it — retry policy, stale-lock sweep, mark_succeeded/failed — gets rewritten.

**2. `strip_cosmetic`'s copyright/page-number regexes** — `apps/api/inplain/worker/handlers/common.py:60-66`, minus the timestamp pattern. ~15 lines of noise suppression that took real iteration to tune. **Delete the `last updated | last modified | updated | effective date | effective` pattern** — verified in the repo, it strips effective dates *before* the SHA and before the diff, so no snapshot retains an effective date and no diff can ever surface "effective date changed 2025-06-01 → 2026-03-14". For a policy-change tracker that is the single most legally meaningful signal in the document, and the spec instructed deleting it as noise.

**3. The citation interaction model** — `apps/web/components/ChangeEventViewer.tsx:12-24, 300-306`, ~40 lines. Citation click → open the enclosing `<details>` → smooth scroll → 2s highlight → fire-and-forget analytics off the interaction path. That behaviour *is* the product. Carry the logic, throw the CSS out, and pin it with a Playwright test before restyling — it currently has zero test coverage.

**4. `_parse_json_object` / `_openrouter_error_detail`** — markdown-fence-stripping and error-envelope unwrapping, ~30 lines, currently forked across `diff.py` and `summarize.py`. Carry one copy into a single LLM client module.

Plus one artifact that is not code: **the 103-class inventory in `globals.css`**. Exactly one class is dead. It is a complete, non-drifted, greppable list of every surface the product has, and it exists nowhere else. Extract it as a surface map before deleting the file. See the design section.

## Carry over with changes

Only one code path qualifies. Everything else is either a decision (below) or a rebuild.

**The HMAC service boundary** — `apps/api/inplain/api/deps.py:60-88` + the signing half in `apps/web/lib/internal-api.ts`. ~100 lines, correct in construction: canonical payload binds timestamp + method + path-with-query + body hash, 300s skew, `hmac.compare_digest`. Verified the payload myself:

```
timestamp \n METHOD \n path \n body_sha256
```

Three required changes, and the first is why the "carry unchanged" instruction had to be rejected:

1. **Sign the principal.** `x-clerk-user-id` and `x-clerk-role` are attached as plain headers *after* signing. A captured request replays for up to 300s with a substituted user id and validates — cross-tenant write on `/internal/documents/watch`. `x-clerk-role: admin` gates the admin routes and is grep-empty across `apps/web`: nothing legitimate ever sets it. Append both to the canonical payload. One line each side.
2. **Add a nonce cache** (or delete the admin routes and accept the 300s window explicitly, in writing). Right now it is neither.
3. **Write down that `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` is a full-impersonation credential.** It is, and nothing says so.

Whether this boundary should exist at all is the biggest open architecture question — see *Open questions*.

## Rebuild

### The data model — do this first, everything else is downstream

`documents.clerk_user_id NOT NULL` with `unique(clerk_user_id, entity_id, doc_type)` is the root defect. Verified. The catalog is 56 public URLs identical for every user, so N watchers of Google produce N document rows, N fetch jobs, N snapshot chains, N diffs, and N identical OpenRouter calls for one real-world event.

Nearly every expensive thing in `refresh` exists to ration that duplication: per-plan check cadence, monthly render quotas, monthly summary quotas, retention-by-tier, `Job.clerk_user_id`, the doc-limit pause/reactivate state machine. Invert the model and **all of it deletes itself**.

Replace with:
- `documents` → one row per `(entity_id, doc_type)`, globally shared, no user column
- `watches(clerk_user_id, entity_id, created_at)` — thin join
- snapshots, diffs, change_events, jobs → all global, all lose `clerk_user_id`
- authz moves from row ownership to a join through `watches`

Two consequences worth naming up front. **Good:** the crawl collapses to 56 fetches/day — a cron job, not a distributed system — and `/companies/[slug]` becomes renderable to signed-out visitors, which is the difference between "a public, indexable, linkable record of what changed in Google's privacy policy" and "a list of 32 company names", which is what ships today (`page.tsx:92`, `changeEvents = userId ? … : []`). **Bad:** "delete my account" can no longer cascade away snapshots, so the immediate-purge promise needs rewording. Shared documents contain no personal data, so this is defensible — but say it.

Also fix at the same time: `notifications` has **no foreign key of any kind** (change_event_id lives in a JSONB payload), and `internal_change_events.py:57` uses `.scalar_one()`, so a dangling notification click-through returns HTTP 500, not 404.

### Retention & lifecycle — the bug that eats the product's only expensive asset

Verified structurally in `cleanup.py:24-35`. A snapshot is written only when the SHA changes, so the previous snapshot is as old as the last *content change* — 6–18 months for a policy. `retention_delete_at` is stamped at write time and never recomputed. Cleanup deletes any expired snapshot not currently `last_snapshot_id`, consulting nothing else. `diffs.from_snapshot_id` and `change_events.diff_id` are both `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the migrations, and nothing anywhere deletes a Diff or ChangeEvent by age.

Compose it: policy unchanged for a year → changes today → diff + change_event + paid LLM summary + notification. Tomorrow's cleanup deletes the year-old from-snapshot → cascade removes the diff → cascade removes the change_event. **The summary you paid for is destroyed within 24 hours, and this is the modal path, not an edge case.** The handler has zero tests and CI never runs `alembic upgrade head`, so no environment has ever observed it.

Rebuild rule: change events get their own retention clock and are never deleted by cascade from a snapshot. Snapshots referenced by a live diff are pinned.

### Change detection & citations

Three verified defects, all approach-level:

- **The materiality gate is duplicated.** `common.py:413-422` runs the full `SequenceMatcher` ratio *and* the full `diff_match_patch` pass, applies its own threshold, and writes `change_score`/`changed_chars` into the job payload. `diff.py:84-86` ignores the payload and recomputes both. The expensive work runs twice per change and the first result is dead data. This is the exact "two implementations of the same thing" disease `CLAUDE.md` says killed `main`, reproduced inside the clean-slate rewrite.
- **Materiality is measured in the wrong units.** A whole-document similarity ratio cannot express "one clause got materially worse." A 67-char "we now sell your personal information" insert into a 65k policy scores ~0.003 and is dropped as cosmetic before a diff job is even enqueued. Gate on absolute changed content — a full sentence of added or removed prose is at minimum *meaningful* — and demote the ratio to a display badge only. Also: the LLM gate is wired to *demote* only, so the one case where a cheap model earns its cost (is this small edit material?) is the case it is never called on. Invert it to promote-only, and persist its reason — a change suppressed with no recorded rationale is unacceptable for a trust product.
- **The citation validator manufactures evidence.** This is the most important finding in the entire review set, because the original assessor said to carry it *verbatim* as "the only thing that distinguishes this product from paste-a-diff-into-ChatGPT." Verified in `summarize.py:440-470`: the fuzzy tier returns `best_chunk` — a *different line from the hunk* — and assigns it to the model's claim without ever rechecking the claim. And `by_id[hid] = added + "\n" + removed` merges both sides into one haystack, so a quote can validate against the removed text while the bullet asserts an addition. Reported reproductions: "sell"→"share", "may not opt out"→"may opt out", "24 months"→"12 months", all emitted as `repaired` and rendered identically to `valid`. Because the nearest-similarity chunk to a removed line is *by construction its replacement*, tier-3 repair preferentially converts a quote into its opposite.

Rebuild: exact match + whitespace/case-tolerant match only. Add `side: "added" | "removed"` to the citation schema and validate against that side alone. Delete fuzzy substitution — no threshold separates a dropped comma from a negation flip, and an honest `unverified` badge beats a confidently wrong quote. Make `repaired` visually distinct or drop the tri-state.

### Capture

Keep the *decisions* (HTTP-first, trafilatura-only with no fallback chain, conditional GET, per-host politeness, SSRF validation with per-hop redirect revalidation). Rebuild the code:

- **Replace the hand-rolled robots parser with `protego`.** ~100 lines implementing RFC 9309 for 32 hosts, with no `*`/`$` wildcard support (`path.startswith(r.path)`), duplicate `User-agent: *` groups silently dropped, prefix-matched UA tokens, and 5xx treated as allow-all. Every one of those fails *open*, against exactly the wildcard-heavy Big Tech robots.txt files in the catalog. One dependency line beats a 100-line RFC implementation. This is textbook KISS.
- **Re-check robots and politeness after every redirect hop.** Currently checked only on `doc.url`; a cross-host 301 means crawling a host you never asked permission from, at unbounded rate, storing the snapshot under a URL that wasn't fetched.
- **Fix conditional GET soundness.** A 304 early-returns before any render/extract path, and `doc.etag` is overwritten with `None` when a 304 omits the header.
- **Stream the response and abort at the size cap** — the 5MB check runs after `resp.content` has already buffered the body.
- **Use `not ip.is_global`** instead of the hand-rolled predicate list, which lets `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT) through today. Pin the resolved IP and connect to it with Host/SNI preserved so httpx cannot re-resolve.
- **Pick one crawler identity.** The pipeline sends a spoofed Chrome UA to origins while evaluating robots against the token `inplain.ai`, which origins never see. Sites are structurally unable to apply rules to this crawler. On a privacy-transparency product that is a launch-day HN comment. Be truthful and accept losing some targets, or stop claiming robots compliance.

### Worker runtime

Keep Postgres-as-queue with `SKIP LOCKED` and queue-scoping via env var — at 56 URLs this is four orders of magnitude inside what it handles, and transactional enqueue (job row committed in the same transaction as the snapshot) is a real property a broker cannot give you. Rebuild the runtime around it:

- **Fix the transaction boundary.** The job's transaction opens on `SELECT Job` and stays open across a robots fetch, a `time.sleep()` politeness delay, up to six HTTP round trips, and (for render) a 45s browser session. Every in-flight job is an idle-in-transaction Postgres connection holding a row lock. Do I/O outside the transaction; open a short one to write the snapshot + child job at the end. Note that the *current* accidental exactly-once property comes from `mark_succeeded` committing handler writes — that contract is undocumented, already violated in two `except` branches, and would be silently lost by a port. Design it in deliberately.
- **Fencing token** (`lock_token uuid` set on claim, required in the mark_* WHERE clause). At-least-once delivery plus non-idempotent handlers plus a 10-minute stale sweep plus an unconditional admin `retry_job` endpoint = duplicate OpenRouter spend and duplicate user notifications, one click away.
- **SIGTERM drain.** Only `KeyboardInterrupt` is handled; every Railway deploy strands up to 10 prefetched jobs in `running` for the full stale window.
- **Dead-letter on recovery** (`attempt >= max_attempts` → `dead`, and reset `run_at`). Today a hung handler cycles every 10 minutes forever, pinning a thread.
- **Per-queue retry policy and real timeouts.** Note honestly: CPython cannot kill a thread, so a per-job wall-clock budget means process-per-job or an event loop. Decide that up front rather than listing it as a checklist item.
- **Idempotency guards**: `run_summarize_job` early-returns if `summary_status` is already completed, before any LLM call; unique index on `notifications(clerk_user_id, change_event_id)`.
- **Prune the jobs table.** Nothing deletes finished jobs outside account deletion; the queue table is also the permanent log, and `/admin/jobs` sorts by an unindexed `created_at`.

### AI summarization

- **One model, chosen by eval.** Seven models across three tiers plus a fourth chain in `diff.py`, none evaluated on a single real policy diff — they were picked by scraping OpenRouter's trending rankings. The entire optimized cost spread is 3 cents per summary against maybe a few hundred summaries a year. Build a 15–20 example golden set from the catalog with hand-written expected bullets and pick from that. Keep at most one fallback, for *outage* only.
- **Catch transport errors specifically.** `except Exception` currently walks to the next model on malformed JSON too, making quality nondeterministic per event.
- **Never raise after the LLM call.** Four raise sites sit outside the model-chain try/except and after the spend; the rollback means `summary_status` stays `pending` and no notify job is ever enqueued. With `temperature=0.0` the same malformed response recurs identically every retry — up to 5 attempts × a 4-model chain of paid calls for a job that provably cannot succeed, ending in a silently stranded change.
- **Pass entity name and doc_type into the prompt** (the classifier already does; the summarizer summarizes an anonymous diff).
- **Record partial coverage.** `_MAX_HUNKS_FOR_LLM = 20` hard-caps input and nothing stores or displays that the summary covered 20 of N hunks. A wholesale rewrite — the change users most need summarized — produces a confidently partial "what changed."
- **Add a prompt-injection guard.** Hunk text is attacker-controlled: anyone whose policy you track can write instructions into it. SPEC claims this is mitigated by "citations required" — the repair path is precisely what defeats that.

### Web tier

Rebuild. ~740 of 3,157 lines are design-independent and every one of them appears on a change list. What actually carries is four ideas, not files: the Clerk route matcher, the HMAC signer, the `<form action={serverAction}>` + hidden inputs + `revalidatePath` mutation pattern, and the 14-route map.

Must not be repeated:
- **Zero tests.** All 56 passing tests are backend — verified. The swallowed-redirect quota bug shipped to Railway precisely because nothing in `apps/web` is executed by a test.
- **No error boundaries.** Verified: no `error.tsx`, no `global-error.tsx`, `notFound()` never called, so `not-found.tsx` is unreachable. A bad slug or a 10s internal timeout renders Next's default error screen — and reports to nobody, because the three Sentry config files are imported by nothing and there is no `instrumentation.ts`.
- **`redirect()` inside a bare `catch {}`.** Verified at `documents.ts:36-43`. Next signals redirects by throwing; the catch swallows it and the check-now call fires anyway. The comment says "worker-side safeguards still apply" — there are none.
- **Writes during GET renders.** `applyEntitlementsToDocuments` POSTs on four read paths with `bestEffort: true` swallowing failures. Amplified by `NotificationBell`, which sits in the root layout and fires a Server Action (a POST that re-renders the route server-side) every 60 seconds — so an idle `/dashboard` tab re-executes a database write plus the full fetch every minute, forever.
- **`await Promise.resolve(params)`** with `params` typed as a sync object. Type it `Promise<{...}>`.
- **Fetch-all-then-filter-in-memory** on the company page and dashboard. Add filtered/cursor-paginated reads — or make them unnecessary by having server components read Postgres directly.
- **Six copies of `clerkEnabled()`**, compensating for `proxy.ts` defaulting to *bypass* when Clerk env is missing. Invert: default protected, bypass on explicit opt-in, delete the six copies.

## Drop

Justified against KISS/YAGNI and against where this is going — a public, indexable record of policy changes for 32 curated companies.

| Drop | Why |
|---|---|
| **Billing, tiers, quotas, entitlements** | ~600 lines by line count, but the tier concept is *schema vocabulary*: `ScheduleTier{daily,6h,1h}` is a persisted per-plan cadence enum, `SummaryStatus.skipped_quota` puts a billing outcome inside the change-event state machine, `retention_for_schedule` makes data retention a function of billing tier inside the worker, and `export/route.ts` encodes plan limits a fifth time. It exists to ration duplicated work that the data-model fix eliminates. It is also unenforced end-to-end today (dead redirect + no API-side quota + client-supplied `schedule_tier` that dispatches the render and summary limits). Delete it; revisit on evidence of demand, and price notifications or API access, never reading public data. |
| **Playwright renderer + `render` queue + render quotas** | 56/56 catalog URLs pass over plain HTTP with trafilatura. Render is enqueued only on HTTP 200 with 1–499 extracted chars; trafilatura returning *nothing* — the actual JS-shell signature — raises and routes to `error` instead. It is unreachable for its own use case, and it costs a fifth Railway service, a 300MB `playwright install` at boot (crash-loop on a network blip), two threads, and a hard `playwright` import in every worker process. Keep a `needs_render` escape hatch in `catalog.json` and re-add only when an entry demands it. |
| **PDF extraction + Tesseract OCR** | Zero PDFs in the catalog and the system binaries are installed on no Railway service — this path has never executed in production. |
| **Self-hosted PostHog + `apps/posthog_proxy` + the 8-event taxonomy** | A whole Railway service and a CSRF workaround app bought funnel analytics for a product with zero users. `PLAN.md` records ~10 consecutive entries of Railway/PostHog firefighting including a self-inflicted outage from `railway down`. Use Postgres counts, or PostHog Cloud free tier, once there is traffic. |
| **Redis** | The only uses are a robots cache for ~40 hosts and a per-host politeness window — the latter a non-atomic GET-then-SET race, the former a Postgres table. The code already falls back to in-memory. Collapse to 3 services: `web`, one Python image running api+worker as two process types, `postgres`. |
| **Alembic as a catalog editor** | Three of six migrations (0003, 0004, 0006) contain no DDL — they are catalog.json data rewrites. Replace with one idempotent upsert-by-slug seed command in the release phase. |
| **`apps/browser-extension` (0 files), `apps/worker` (a README), `app/sw.js`** | Empty directories and a tombstone service worker for a PWA that was never registered. Pure archaeology. |
| **The second Clerk webhook receiver** | Two receivers, two tiers, two secrets, two verification libraries, split only by event type. Keep the FastAPI one (`user.deleted` cleanup is real). |
| **Side-by-side and section diff modes** | Section grouping is a client-side regex guessing headings from 200 chars of diff text with a `General changes N` fallback — and trafilatura discards heading markup entirely, so it is *always* degenerate, not sometimes. Ship unified only. If sections matter, the extractor emits them. |
| **The `@hey-api/openapi-ts` obligation** | Never installed. The API types `diff_hunks` and both summary bullet arrays as `list[dict[str, Any]]`, so codegen would emit `Record<string, unknown>` for the three shapes the product depends on. Hand-written types are the *correct* outcome — bless it, and fix the Pydantic models. |
| **Launch ceremony** | §16 launch plan, L1–L15, §15.2 polish checklist, §13 risk register, §5.10 threat model. All fifteen milestones are marked Done against a product with no users and, as it turns out, a fail-open robots parser and a citation validator that fabricates evidence. That definition of "done" is the thing most worth not carrying. |

## The design overhaul

The owner is right, and the assessors were both half right. **The output is slop and every value in it dies. The architecture underneath is correct and should be kept.** Those are separable, and conflating them is what produced the disagreement.

### What specifically reads as slop

Verified in the repo: 1,007 lines of CSS, **57** `var(--)` references against **84** raw `rgba()` literals — the ten-token layer is bypassed more often than it is used. **115** inline `style={{}}` objects across 18 files, **8** literal `<div style={{height: N}} />` spacers. No spacing scale (15 values, dominant unit 10px), no type scale (15 sizes including 12.5px, 13.5px, 15.5px — half-pixel eyeballing), font weights 750 and 760 on a face whose axis maxes at 700, so three "distinct" weights render identically. Container width duplicated in five places. **Zero** `:focus-visible` rules and **zero** `prefers-color-scheme` blocks in the whole file.

The aesthetic is the 2023 AI-startup landing kit: cream body with radial gradient blobs, backdrop-blur glass header, `border-radius: 999px` on eleven things including text inputs, `translateY(-1px)` lift on every button, a hero entrance animation, hot-orange accent, wonk-serif + geometric-sans display pairing. Twenty-seven of 103 classes (~27% of the rule blocks) are pure marketing chrome — `hero*`, `preview*`, `step*`, `cta*`, `pricing*` — and nearly all of the "template signature" lives there.

**And the diff — the entire product — is styled as a card, not as a diff.** 14px geometric display sans set on legal prose with no measure constraint, no monospace option, no line numbers, no gutter, no word-level intra-line marks. Both `.diffAdded` and `.diffRemoved` explicitly declare `text-decoration: none`, deliberately removing the one redundant non-colour cue, and their backgrounds compute to **1.05:1** against each other — separable by hue alone. Both also set `overflow-wrap: anywhere` *and* `word-break: break-word`, breaking words mid-token on a long-form reading surface for 100% of users. It has strictly less fidelity than `git diff` in a terminal.

### What to build instead

**Positioning: a reference instrument, not a launch page.** The correct comparables are a court docket, a well-made changelog, `git log`. Not a SaaS homepage. Every decision below follows from that.

- **Delete the marketing 27% entirely.** Once change events are public and indexable, the homepage is *the live change feed* — the most recent policy changes across all 32 companies, with dates, diffs, and summaries. That is both the product and the SEO surface. A hero with three feature cards is worse than the actual data.
- **Typography: two faces, both chosen for reading.** One text face for prose (a real text serif or a humanist sans — not Fraunces, not Space Grotesk; both are display faces doing a text job), one mono for the diff gutter and code-like content. Kill the wonk-serif/geometric-sans personality pairing: this is a legal-reference tool where legibility *is* the brand. Measure constrained to 66–75ch on every prose surface. Real leading rhythm. Delete `text-rendering: geometricPrecision` from `body` — it is an SVG-scaling hint.
- **Colour: near-monochrome, one accent, reserved.** The accent is for citations and nothing else — it is the summary→evidence control and it should be the only coloured thing on the page. Currently that control is the *smallest, lowest-contrast* element on the page: 3.08:1 at ~10.9px. Diff green/red become a secondary channel, never the sole cue.
- **The diff surface gets hand-authored CSS and a real design.** `+`/`−` gutter, line numbers, monospace option, tuned leading, no word-breaking. **Add word-level intra-line highlighting** — the backend already emits `added`/`removed` arrays, and this single change raises the tool's value more than any amount of styling. Track it as a feature, not a restyle; it has a backend contract question attached.
- **Design light and dark simultaneously.** Not a token swap: diff fills, the citation accent, and the focus ring all need separately chosen dark values or contrast regresses. For a tool people read long legal text in, dark mode is not decoration.
- **Add `@media print`.** There are zero print rules and an `/export` route. A legal-evidence tool whose users print a diff currently gets a glass header, radial gradients and translucent surfaces on paper.

### What structure survives underneath

**Keep the architecture: semantic classes plus CSS custom properties, one stylesheet, zero CSS framework.** I side with the challenger here, against Tailwind, for two reasons the assessor did not weigh:

1. **Tailwind would not have prevented a single measured defect.** The two dominant offenders — `marginTop: 10` (×23) and `marginTop: 6` (×19) — are `mt-2.5` and `mt-1.5` in Tailwind v4's default scale. Both *on-scale*. `<div className="h-4.5"/>` is still a spacer div. `mt-[18px]` is legal by design. And all eight accessibility failures survive a migration untouched. The sprawl came from nobody deciding, not from a missing scale, and a framework does not decide.
2. **The owner will iterate on design again.** Semantic CSS makes a re-skin a one-file change. Utilities in markup make every re-skin an 18-file refactor, permanently. Choosing the architecture that makes the *next* redesign expensive, in order to fix a redesign that is happening anyway, optimizes the wrong axis. Adding `tailwindcss` + `@tailwindcss/postcss` + `lightningcss` native binaries to a 5-dependency, zero-advisory, no-CSS-build app for ~10 screens fails KISS on its own terms.

What the challenger got wrong is that discipline alone fixes it. It doesn't. Two additions make the architecture actually hold:

- **Put the scales in the token layer.** ~30 lines of `--space-*`, `--text-*`, `--weight-*`, `--z-*`, `--motion-*`, plus semantic state colours (`--diff-added`, `--diff-removed`, `--citation`, `--focus-ring`). That delivers everything Tailwind was being imported for, for zero dependencies, in the file that already exists.
- **Add the gate that was missing.** This is the real root cause. SPEC §15.3 already mandates ≥4.5:1 contrast, visible focus indicators, and "no content conveyed by color alone (especially in diffs)". SPEC §16.1 marks **L2 "UI polish pass — Done"** and **L12 "Diff viewer finalized — Done"**. So the system was specified, violated on exactly those three points, and signed off as complete. Rebuilding the CSS without fixing the sign-off reproduces the failure in nicer class names. The gate: a stylelint rule banning raw `px`/`rgba` outside the token block, and a Playwright + axe run in CI. There is currently no frontend job in CI at all and **9 ARIA attributes in the entire frontend**.

**Extract the 103-class inventory before deleting the file.** One class is dead; there are no duplicate forks and no `enhanced-`/`-v2` parallel stack — the precise disease `main` died of. About 50 of those names are product-specific (`hunk*`, `diff*`, `citation*`, `summary*`, `company*`, `bell*`, `skeleton*`, `policyTextBox`, `tableWrap`). That is a complete list of every surface the new design must cover, and it exists nowhere else. It is the most useful single input to the redesign and both reviewers came close to throwing it away.

### Non-negotiable floor — must not be repeated

Measured, not guessed. Every one of these ships today:

1. **Colour is the sole cue on the diff** (1.05:1, strikethrough explicitly removed, no "Added"/"Removed" labels outside split mode). Flat WCAG 1.4.1 failure on the core surface, affecting ~8% of men. Add text labels and a `+`/`−` gutter.
2. **Citations fail AA** — 3.08:1 at ~10.9px, on the primary summary→evidence control.
3. **Zero `:focus-visible` rules.** `outline: none` replaced by a 14%-alpha box-shadow, nowhere near 3:1. No skip link. The entire company directory grid has hover styling and no focus styling.
4. **The diff-mode switcher is invisible to assistive tech** — three plain buttons, active state conveyed only by a 14% background tint, no `aria-pressed`, no `role="tablist"`.
5. **`role="menu"` on a div of divs** in the notification bell — no arrow keys, no Escape, no focus return, no trap, no outside-click. A wrong role is worse than none. The badge count has no `aria-live`, so a screen-reader user never learns a notification arrived.
6. **Reduced-motion covers only the hero** — it misses every hover transform, the *infinite* skeleton pulse, and `scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"})`, which are the two that actually trigger vestibular issues.
7. **`100vh` not `100dvh`** — the iOS Safari toolbar jump.
8. **Directory filters are client state only** — no `?q=`/`?category=` URL sync, so filtered views are unshareable and un-back-buttonable, and no `aria-live` result count. For a reference tool that is a structural miss, not a visual one, and it is a routing fix, not a CSS fix.
9. **No `aria-current="page"`** anywhere in the nav.
10. **The CSP sets `object-src`/`base-uri`/`frame-ancestors` but no `style-src`** — 115 inline style objects permanently foreclose tightening it on an app with auth. Removing them is a security win, not only an aesthetic one.

---

## Sequencing

**Phase 0 — Decide, before any code (1–2 days).**
Rewrite SPEC from scratch, ~600 lines, using the old one as source material. Do *not* port and edit it — the frame is the defect, and "preserve §12 verbatim" is actively harmful because the new design reverses at least eight of its rows (Pro $9/Business $29, PH/HN launch, blue-green deploys, pypdf+Tesseract, static homepage, in-app-notifications-only). Rewrite §12 **with a status column: upheld / reversed / never implemented**. Keep verbatim: §1.4 non-goals (the best page in the repo, and the reason the frontend has five dependencies), Appendix B's queue SQL, the column vocabulary (`etag`/`last_modified`, the robots triple, `extract_version`, `summary_status`). Settle the two forks in *Open questions* here. **Blocks everything.**

**Phase 1 — Data model (2–3 days).** Entity-scoped documents + `watches`. One generated `0001` migration plus an idempotent seed command. Real FKs on `notifications`, `last_snapshot_id` as a proper FK with `ON DELETE SET NULL`, change-event retention decoupled from snapshot cascade. Declare `ON DELETE` in the models, and make CI run `alembic upgrade head` and assert an empty autogenerate diff — the migrations and the ORM currently disagree on all 8 FKs and the test DB is built from `create_all`, so production's cascade semantics are untested. **Blocks: worker, capture, summarize, web, auth. Nothing else starts first.**

**Phase 2 — Worker runtime + capture (1 week, parallel-safe after Phase 1).** Queue runtime with fencing, drain, dead-lettering, and I/O outside the transaction. Capture with `protego`, per-hop robots, streaming size cap, pinned-IP transport, one honest crawler identity. Delete render and PDF/OCR here. **Blocks: diff, summarize.**

**Phase 3 — Detection, diff, summarization (1 week).** One materiality gate in one place. Word-level diff marks (backend contract — decide granularity here, it blocks the diff UI). One eval-chosen model. Rebuilt citation validator with `side`. **Blocks: the diff UI.**

**Phase 4 — Web structure (1 week).** Routing, server actions, public company pages, error boundaries, `notFound()`, a `/changes` timeline route (the product loop is "come back when something changed" and there is currently no route for that). Land the *non-visual* fixes here on whatever markup exists — error boundaries, the watch flow, the killed entitlement writes, HMAC identity binding. **If they wait for the redesign they get re-litigated as design decisions and lost in the churn.** Add the first web tests in this phase, not after.

**Phase 5 — Design (1–2 weeks, overlaps Phase 4).** Brand/type/colour decision → token layer with scales → surface-by-surface rebuild against the extracted class inventory → the diff surface last, because it is the one place visual design and product logic are the same decision and it depends on Phase 3's word-diff contract. Land the stylelint + axe CI gate *before* the surface work, not after. Migrate atomically per route: a half-migration with new classes alongside surviving inline styles is worse than either endpoint.

**Explicit blocks:**
- Data model → everything. There is no useful work that survives doing it second.
- Word-diff contract (Phase 3) → diff UI (Phase 5).
- Brand/type decision → token layer → all UI. This is upstream of code and can be decided during Phases 1–3.
- Clerk's hosted components (`SignInButton`, `UserButton`) carry their own appearance layer and must be themed, or the new design breaks at the auth boundary.
- The CI gate (typecheck + `alembic upgrade head` + a frontend test job + axe) should exist before Phase 2, not at the end. Its absence is why every finding above survived to a deploy.

## Open questions for the owner

1. **Public-first forces email into scope. Accept that?** If change events are public and there is no billing, the entire signed-in surface is a watchlist plus in-app notifications a user only sees if they return unprompted. Email is then the *only* conversion event and the only reason auth exists. SPEC non-goal #4 says no email. Going public-first means promoting email to core scope, or accepting that accounts have almost no purpose.

2. **Does the BFF survive?** The worker never calls the HTTP API — verified. So ~1,100 lines of FastAPI routes, HMAC on both sides, a hand-mirrored TS type layer with no codegen, and two Clerk webhook receivers exist solely to move rows into a React server component. Six separate findings (both N+1s, fetch-all-then-filter, entitlement write-on-read, unsigned identity, and the need for boundaries around 10s network timeouts) dissolve if server components read Postgres directly. **My recommendation: collapse it.** Python keeps the schema and the pipeline (trafilatura anchors extraction to Python); Next gets read-only DB access for public catalog/timeline reads; writes (watch, unwatch, check-now) go through three signed endpoints. The honest cost is two languages against one schema — mitigate by keeping SQLAlchemy as the single source of truth and generating or hand-mirroring only the three write DTOs. This is the largest single simplification available and it should be decided in Phase 0.

3. **Publishing full policy text, or only hunks?** §2.6 promises signed-out visitors "latest policy text" for documents of 24k–210k chars. That is wholesale public republication of copyrighted works across 56 URLs — categorically larger exposure than publishing a diff hunk plus commentary. **My recommendation: hunks + summary + a link to source, never a full mirror.** But it is your call and it must be made before the public pages are built.

4. **Is there a revenue timeline?** Deleting billing is right on the evidence and re-adding it is roughly a week, not a day. If there is a launch date with a paid tier attached, say so now — it is the one recommendation here that a business constraint could legitimately override.

5. **Does any Railway data need to survive?** The plan assumes no. If it does, the data-model inversion becomes a real migration rather than a reset, and that changes Phases 1–2 substantially.

6. **Before the history purge: re-run classification over the existing snapshot pairs.** That number tells you how many real policy changes the deployed system silently dropped as cosmetic, and whether it ever actually worked. It is worth knowing, and the purge erases the evidence.
